de4beaf9c5834c50cd06b8fd7e31ba973b19240b.summary: A WIRED news article published 11 July 2019 reports that Magecart, a group of card-skimming hackers, has hit 17,000 domains in the past few months by casting a wide net for vulnerable ecommerce sites. The article says Magecart has been behind hacks of British Airways and Ticketmaster, and warns that the method could lead to even bigger problems.

actors.q: Magecart has been behind some of the bigger hacks of the past few years
actors.by: the report itself (WIRED article by Brian Barrett)

sectors.q: widest possible net to find vulnerable ecommerce sites

techniques.q: all with the singular goal of stealing credit card numbers

figures.q: they’ve managed to hit 17,000 domains in the past few months alone

hedges: The article says the group's method could lead to even bigger problems.

de6ff68c9908a3cf753f53848cf5e0171db665a8.summary: DataBreaches.Net reports that the AlphV group, also called BlackCat, added Hampton-Newport News CSB to its leak site in November 2023. It claimed to have stolen over 800 GB of sensitive client and employee data and threatened to publish it and spam customers after a 48-hour deadline. The article criticises the group and urges it to delete the data.
